title: kv-cache-spillover-compaction-eviction-heuristics-v19
author: Aisha Thompson
description:
Context: long-running inference pods show degraded throughput and increased tail latency under mixed short/long prompt workloads caused by KV cache fragmentation and unbounded spillover paging. This PR implements the v19 heuristics: fragmentation-aware eviction, adaptive compaction thresholds, and async spillover paging with backpressure to the scheduler.

Motivation: previous heuristics evicted by least-recently-used (LRU) at shard granularity which failed for fragmented per-request KV footprints. Under sustained load we observed memory amplification and OOMs on 80B model pods. The goal is to reduce tail allocations, cut paging churn, and keep continuous batching performant under memory pressure.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a fragmentation score per KV-entry and integrates it into the eviction priority (age + size + fragmentation).
- Adds an async spillover pager that batches host-memory writes and reads to reduce small I/O operations and schedule-aware prefetching for active batches.
- Implements adaptive compaction: compact when free-frag ratio > 0.25 or after N evictions on the same region; tuneable via runtime flags.
- Adds backpressure signals to the continuous batching scheduler so that when pager queues exceed thresholds, new low-priority requests are throttled or routed to fallback model variants.
- Adds diagnostic counters and histograms (frag_score, pager_queue_depth, compaction_runs) and a per-route eviction-policy tag for observability.

Benchmarks: (internal microbench on p4d with 8 concurrent clients, mixed prompt lengths)
- Peak memory tail reduced by ~28% compared to v18 heuristics.
- 95th token latency reduced from 210ms -> 165ms for mixed workloads.
- Paging IOPS reduced by ~62% due to batching in the async pager.
- Throughput under heavy long-seq load improved by ~12% (tokens/s).

Backward compatibility and rollout: default heuristics remain the same via feature flag `kv.eviction.v19.enabled=false`. We tested a canary rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback when pager_queue_depth > 200 for >30s.

Testing and safety: added unit tests for frag scoring and compaction triggers, e2e bench harness tests that compare v18 vs v19 under synthetic workloads, and a chaos test that simulates host paging latency spikes. All tests run in CI (see checks).

Related: Linear ENG-2145, ENG-2410; Jira SUP-892 for an incident that motivated this change.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2145)
- [x] Benchmarks added to perf suite
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan included
- [x] Observability and alerts added

Notes: further follow-ups planned to tune compaction cost model and integrate with the allocator's placement heuristics.
